== Biography ==
{{Ireland Native}}
{{Migrating Ancestor | origin = Ireland | destination = United States | origin-flag = Flags-1.gif | destination-flag = US_Flags-1.png}}

William Glasgow was born around 1799.<ref>Based on his death in January 1855 at the age of 55.</ref> He was from Killycurragh, near Cookstown, County Tyrone, where he served as a ruling elder in the First Cookstown Presbyterian Church before emigrating to the United States.<ref name="d"/>

An obituary in the ''Belfast Mercury'' notes: "January 21, at Sandusky City, State of Ohio, United States, Mr. William Glasgow, formerly of Killyenrugh, near Cookstown, aged 56 years. He was for many years (previous to his emigration) a ruling elder in the congregation of First Cookstown."

William passed away on 21 January 1855 in Sandusky, Ohio.<ref name="d">[https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/viewer/bl/0000784/18550404/021/0002 "Deaths"], ''Belfast Mercury'' - Wednesday 04 April 1855, Page 2</ref>

There is speculation that he may be a missing son of [[Glasgow-822|John Glasgow (1767-1851)]].
=== Marriage and children ===

William married [[Glendinning-340|Nancy Glendinning]], described in the 1903 Glendinning memorial as the fifth daughter, with mother Mary Bell and birth in April 1803. The memorial calls William a farmer and businessman of Killycorragh and names their eight children:<ref name="GlendinningMemorial1903">''A Brief Memorial of the Deceased Members of the Glendinning Family, from the Siege of Derry to the Present Time'' (1903), [https://glendinning.name/history/irish_glendinning.pdf#page=17 PDF p.17], without a printed page number; cover and page visually verified 24 October 2026. Retrospective family publication.</ref>

* [[Glasgow-3148|Henry Cunningham Glasgow]]
* [[Glasgow-3151|Adam Glasgow]], whose later adult identity remains qualified below
* [[Glasgow-3149|Isaac Watts Glasgow]]
* [[Glasgow-3150|Benjamin Glasgow]]
* [[Glasgow-2825|Alexander Flemming Glasgow]], recorded with that spelling
* [[Glasgow-3158|Mary Glasgow]]
* [[Glasgow-3146|Matilda Glasgow]]
* [[Glasgow-3147|Jane Glasgow]]

The sons and daughters are listed separately; their order does not establish an interleaved birth sequence or dates. The memorial refers to sons’ long railway service and the Nickleplate line without identifying the sons concerned. It records Nancy’s death at Belle Center on 20 March 1890, aged 87. That reported age and April 1803 birth are recorded here as the book’s statements, without deriving a new birthday.<ref name="GlendinningMemorial1903" />

== Research Notes ==
=== Earlier ancestry and the named son Adam ===

The memorial gives no father or other Glasgow kin for William. His father remains unknown; the suggested [[Glasgow-822|John Glasgow]] connection is unproved. Its explicit son Adam establishes a child role in the William/Nancy family, but does not settle the adult identity represented by [[Glasgow-3151|Adam Glasgow]]. That father-profile pair remains 77% probable because the 1834/1840 birth claims and a competing Ohio-born [[Glasgow-2387|Adam]], son of Arthur, remain unresolved. No merger or child birth date follows from the list.<ref name="GlendinningMemorial1903" />

=== The Ohio death notices ===

The Belfast News-Letter reports William’s death on 21 January 1855 at Sandusky City, Ohio, aged 55, and describes him as formerly of Killycurragh near Cookstown and a ruling elder of First Cookstown before emigrating.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/390549257/ Belfast News-Letter, 2 April 1855, p.2].</ref> The attributed Belfast Mercury notice gives age 56. Both reported ages should be retained; they do not establish an exact birthday. His 1855 death excludes him as the living William Glasgow who testified as uncle of the Cookstown mill plaintiffs in July 1858.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/390574459/ Belfast News-Letter, 22 July 1858, p.3].</ref>
